title: Us-vs-Them bias in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to complete sentences starting with 'We are' (ingroup) and 'They are' (outgroup), then scoring the generated sentences for ingroup solidarity and outgroup hostility using an LLM-as-a-judge based on Social Identity Theory. The texts are further analyzed using allotaxonometry, rank-turbulence divergence, and dictionary-based sentiment dynamics.

Conditioning language models with U.S. political personas (Conservative vs. Liberal) to evaluate how partisan framing affects the magnitude and direction of 'us-vs-them' bias. This is measured via embedding regression to quantify contextual semantic shifts, along with lexical and sentiment divergence between persona outputs.
